Our Aims and Values
Context
Parsons Green Prep (PGP) is a leading day standalone co-educational 4-11 London prep school that offers both a challenging and rich curriculum and a broad range of opportunity experienced within the context of a happy childhood.
PGP is committed to promoting an education that inspires the pupils in Years 1-6 and children in early years to achieve their best within a rich, happy, safe and fulfilling school experience upon which to ensure rapid progress and build future success.
Amplifying potential | Inspiring futures
The school aims to amplify potential by inspiring a love of learning in a safe, stimulating and harmonious environment where respect for all, a sense of social responsibility and pupils’ emotional wellbeing are prioritised. Pupils are encouraged to develop as creative, curious and critical thinkers who embrace challenge and strive for excellence in all that they do.

About Us
Parsons Green Prep is a selective, co-educational, independent prep school for children aged 4 to 11 years, in classes from Reception to Year 6. Known to our families as PGP, our building and grounds are in the heart of Fulham, a stone’s throw from Parsons Green.
Described by the Good Schools Guide as a ‘hidden gem’, we are small enough for every child to be noticed, valued and appreciated by everyone. Our academic ambitions are high, with excellent 11+ results year after year, and our facilities are the envy of many competitor schools. Our children behave beautifully and treat each other with kindness and respect and our parent body is creative, supportive and extremely welcoming.
Who Are the Leaders and Staff at Parsons Green Prep?
PGP has all the benefits of a single proprietor prep school with a well-informed leadership and governance team who effectively keep the focus of children’s development at the heart of their decision making. We combine academic ambition and traditional values with strong pastoral care and the promotion of pupils’ wellbeing. This tailored and individual approach enables children to flourish and succeed.
We would love to meet you. Please do take the opportunity to visit the school and experience how PGP would be for your child. You can Zoom the Head or come for an individual or group tour whenever it suits you. Admissions is waiting to take your call.

Head’s Welcome
Welcome to Parsons Green Prep.
It is my privilege to lead a school that combines academic excellence with a deep commitment to the happiness and wellbeing of every child. Parsons Green Prep is a place where children are known as individuals, encouraged to be ambitious and given the confidence to embrace challenges, discover their strengths and develop a genuine love of learning.
The very best schools nurture the whole child. Academic success is important and our pupils are exceptionally well prepared for the next stage of their education. Equally important, however, is the development of character: kindness, resilience, curiosity and integrity. Our aim is that every child leaves PGP not only with strong academic foundations, but also with the confidence and self-belief to thrive in an ever-changing world.
The aspect that makes our school particularly special is its sense of community. As a proudly independent school with a single proprietor, we know our pupils exceptionally well and provide the individual attention that allows each child to flourish. The relationships between pupils, staff and families are central to school life and create an environment in which children feel secure, supported and valued.
I am especially proud that our most recent ISI inspection recognised pupils’ emotional wellbeing as a Significant Strength of the school. This rare accolade reflects the importance we place on ensuring that every child feels happy, understood and able to succeed. Inspectors noted the exceptional impact of the school’s wellbeing provision and the maturity with which pupils understand both their own emotional wellbeing and that of others.
There is a wonderful energy about PGP, a school where children are encouraged to think independently, participate fully and make the most of every opportunity. It is a community built on respect, where childhood is celebrated and where pupils are inspired to achieve their very best.
I would be delighted to welcome you to the school and share with you the many qualities that make it such a happy and inspiring place to learn.
Alex Jarrett Head Parsons Green Prep

Our History
On 21 March 1804 there are references in The Times of the sale of Fulham Lodge, a villa which stood in extensive gardens to the south of Fulham Road. Today the school stands in part of those gardens. Fulham Lodge was the home of Miss Eliza Carey, an actor, and a favourite haunt of Fredrick, Duke of York, son of George III. Fulham Lodge was pulled down in 1847 and various houses built on the land, including a new Fulham Lodge which would later be renamed Eridge House. The house was bought by Mr John Glenny, an outfitter with a shop on the Strand, who was the brother of George Glenny who owned the extensive fruit and vegetable nursery in the open fields on the north side of Fulham Road.
The building was then purchased by Mr Fredrick Wright in 1867 and renamed Eridge House. It is not entirely certain why he chose the new name, but the most likely explanation is that the Wrights came from Sussex. There is historical evidence to show they had connections with the High Weald region, where Eridge Rocks is a beautiful area of woodland and sandstone rocks.
Eridge House survived the Blitz in WWII when bombs landed close by along the Fulham Road and around Putney Bridge. Since then it has been both a private residence and, because of its considerable size, an office for a department of Fulham and Hammersmith Council. It was put up for sale in 2001 and purchased by the present owner who converted the building for use as a school.
Eridge House School grew rapidly with extensions to the original building on the north and western facades. New classrooms, a IT suite and the school hall were added to the existing building which houses the expansive Reception classroom and early years outdoor learning environment, a library, Science, Technology, Engineering, Arts and Mathematics (STEAM) room, music room, and further classrooms. The building has considerable outdoor space with an Astroturf pitch for sport alongside designated play areas. It has many old and well-established trees dating back to its garden days. The school changed its name to Parsons Green Prep in 2014, but the name Eridge House can still be seen on the original front gate.
Today, the school has become one of the leading prep schools in West London.

Posted: 10th June 2026
Introduction
Parsons Green Prep (PGP) are delighted to introduce our new wraparound care provision, developed in response to the growing needs of our school community. We recognise that modern family life often requires flexibility, and that many parents balance busy working schedules alongside school commitments. Our aim is to provide a safe, nurturing and enriching environment beyond the standard school day – offering both support for parents and a positive, engaging experience for all of our pupils from Reception – Year 6.
Morning Care
Children are welcomed into morning care where they can play games, read and socialise with friends, providing a gentle and positive start to the day.
After-School Care
After-School Care sessions run from the end of each year group’s lessons until 18:00, allowing for a seamless transition from the school day or club into a relaxing and enjoyable after-school environment.
Until 17.00, the children will have the opportunity to either attend a PGP club or PGP’s Focus Club to finish homework, read and complete various structured tasks.
Chill Club begins at 17.00 where the children will be offered board games, craft activities and the opportunity to socialise with friends. For those staying after 17:00, the school will provide a range of healthy foods and snacks such as wraps, cold platters and fruit provided by our caterer, Thomas Franks.
For the safety and wellbeing of our pupils, legal ratios are strictly observed and therefore there is a need to know the number of children booked in wrap around care 24 hours in advance.
Sibling Club
For pupils in Reception, Year 1 or Year 2, who have a sibling in the Prep school, sibling club will run free of charge from the end of their lessons, to Prep dismissal at 16.00. If the Reception, Year 1 or Year 2 child participates in a PGP club, as does their sibling, they will be invited to remain in sibling club free of charge from the end of their club until 17.00 when the Prep club finishes. If a child is not participating in a PGP club, they will be admitted into wraparound care at the prices listed above. Please see the Parent Handbook for further details.
A Safe and Supportive Environment
Our wraparound care is delivered by qualified, paediatric first-aid trained and experienced members of staff who know our pupils well, ensuring a familiar, secure and caring atmosphere. The provision reflects our school values, supporting children’s wellbeing, independence and social development in a relaxed and happy setting.
We are excited to offer this enhanced provision and look forward to continuing to support our parent community with this new initiative.

Year 1 to Year 6 Curriculum
What Does the Year 1–6 Curriculum Cover at Parsons Green Prep?
We believe that how a child learns is as important as what a child learns. Our teaching techniques reflect the latest pedagogical research. We want children to develop research and presentational skills, to question and to justify what they hear and say. Pair work and partner talk are used extensively and higher-order thinking skills are developed with open-ended and ‘what if?’ questioning.
We teach from whole to parts, simple to complex and concrete to abstract. We offer our children an extensive and challenging education in breadth, depth and richness. Our children are well taught and thoroughly prepared for their next school and many achieve well above national expectations.
How Are Assessment and Record-Keeping Used to Personalise Learning?
At Parsons Green Prep we believe that assessment and record keeping are an essential part of school life. Much of what teachers do in classrooms can be described as assessment, from questioning the children to observing what they say and do. It is the interactions between learners and teachers within lessons that shape the next steps for improvement. Assessment is important because it enables teachers to monitor the progress of individual pupils and to plan effectively for all pupils. It is also how pupils understand what they have achieved and what they need to work on. In addition, GL Assessments are administered throughout the year, providing each cohort with scores for their cognitive abilities including for VR (verbal reasoning), NVR (non-verbal reasoning), reading and spelling, as well as nationally benchmarked, standardised scores in English and maths.
For new pupils that start within the academic year, there is a baseline assessment for English and maths to ensure that teaching enables the child to access the curriculum and for them to be stretched. Previous school reports will also be used to ascertain strengths and starting points.
The humanities
The humanities aim to give children a rich and varied experience that develops their key skills and knowledge and broadens their interests. We encourage a cross-curricular approach to strengthen and consolidate learning, positively impacting on children’s understanding of topics. Themed learning with cross-curricular links enables children to have a deeper understanding of the topic. At the start of the topic the children are asked two key questions: what do you already know about the topic and what would you like to find out?
Science, Technology, Engineering, Arts and Maths (STEAM)
Ask a child to solve a maths problem, and you have supported them through their next assessment. Ask a child to explore the universe with you, build a rocket and see how maths is an integral part of this process, and you have captured their curiosity. This is what our STEAM initiative is all about. It brings science, technology, engineering, the arts and maths to life and gives purpose and real meaning to learning in the classroom. STEAM is designed to capture the enthusiasm young children have for science and empirical discovery and develop this into a lasting interest in STEAM subjects.
Whether making balloon-powered cars or a bridge made out of newspaper, it is an opportunity for children to solve problems, design, create and explain. Through STEAM, pupils develop a valuable set of skills including teamwork, resilience, reasoning and critical and creative thinking.
STEAM at PGP is promoted in a variety of ways, including the STEAM curriculum, assemblies, STEAM-themed days and workshops. Outside speakers are invited to the school to enhance the children’s learning experience. They come from a variety of backgrounds; their enthusiasm and commitment encourage young people to engage in STEAM and to see the career possibilities that come from learning and linking STEAM subjects.
English
English
Through English, we develop our ability to listen, speak, read and write. These fundamental life skills enable children to express themselves fluently and creatively and give them the foundation they need to become enthusiastic, lifelong readers and writers. English forms part of the Humanities. Reading and writing skills are developed and nurtured in conjunction with different topic work, giving the children the opportunity to improve their skills in a variety of different contexts. Children’s English skills are developed through constant support and encouragement, starting in the Early Years and continuing as children progress through the school.
In Pre-prep and Prep, English skills are taught in dedicated daily lessons. These sessions typically cover a reading or a writing activity, a focused word or sentence activity, a guided group or independent activity or a whole class session for reviewing progress and learning. Children develop important skills, learning to talk to adults as well as their peers. They are taught to listen carefully to expand their vocabulary and are also shown how to explore words in texts. Children from Year 1 upwards have a smooth transition from the free-flow ethos in Reception to a graduated introduction to spelling, punctuation and grammar skills lessons, as well as the opportunity to apply taught skills during daily independent writing sessions. Children are shown self-evaluation techniques. They are given the tools to begin planning, drafting and evaluating their own work.
The children enjoy putting their English skills into action at our special school events, including readathons, spelling bees, book fairs and author visits. World Book Day provides another exciting opportunity for us to enthuse our young learners, with the whole school taking part in themed events. Weekly class assemblies, school productions and ‘buddy’ reading activities also develop speaking and listening skills and help the children to gain confidence by performing for an audience.
Parsons Green Prep – School Reading List 20250430
Maths
Maths
Through maths, we seek to challenge and extend children in their mathematical thinking as well as supporting and emphasising the key skills of STEAM. Children are taught a broad base of mathematical knowledge and skills. We teach to each child’s individual needs, supporting or extending them where appropriate and catering for all children across the learning spectrum.
In Pre-prep, children develop a knowledge and understanding of maths through visual, auditory and kinaesthetic teaching and learning. They learn to count, read, write and order numbers to 100 and beyond. They develop a range of mental calculation skills and are encouraged to use these confidently in different settings. They learn about shape and space through practical activities that help their understanding of the environment. They are introduced to mathematical language and encouraged to use it to explain methods and reasoning when solving problems.
In Prep, children are taught to use and apply number skills more confidently. They move from counting with ease to calculating with all four number operations. They are taught strategies to try and solve problems with mental methods before using other approaches. We explore features of shape and space, and develop measuring skills in a range of contexts. They gain confidence in discussing and presenting their reasoning and methods, using a wide range of mathematical terms, diagrams and charts. The idea of ‘working mathematically’ is fostered from the start across all strands of learning.
Science
Science
An understanding of science starts with an inquiring mind. Our primary aim is to harness each child’s natural inquisitiveness and develop their scientific skills, knowledge and understanding of the world. Children enjoy a wealth of resources in the STEAM room. They are encouraged to work scientifically by asking scientific questions, using scientific vocabulary, planning and carrying out investigations and analysing their results. We aim to build key knowledge and science skills and carry out practical investigations, encouraging their curiosity and making learning exciting.
The children get involved in ‘real’ scientific activities. These include preparing and undertaking science experiments, solving everyday problems linked to current affairs, visiting local science museums, gardens and environmental centres, and participating in recycling and ecological initiatives. They also hear from members of scientific groups and various science educators who are invited to speak and share their experiences with the children.
At Parsons Green Prep we use a variety of teaching and learning styles in our science lessons, which are adapted to support all the learning needs within the class. The children work in pairs and in small groups to encourage discussion. They are tasked with inquiry-based research activities. Each term, we have whole school activities linked to the science curriculum. One particularly exciting example was a project to hatch chicks – their progress was broadcast to the classrooms and school hall via a live weblink. The children enjoy whole school science days and workshops through the year.
Computing
Computing
We support and extend the children in computing skills and aim to provide them with the relevant knowledge they will need for the future. We follow the new National Curriculum for computing. This has three main areas: computer science, information technology and digital literacy.
Computing is not a standalone subject. While it is taught as a dedicated lesson to everyone, computing also features as a part of many other lessons, whether preparing a presentation in French or putting together a spreadsheet in maths. Computer literacy is taken for granted at the majority of senior schools and we expect our pupils to achieve a good level of proficiency before they leave PGP. Good technological resources enable teachers to enhance learning and teach computing skills effectively.
Teachers use a range of strategies to deliver computing. These include whole-class demonstrations using classroom Smartboards, individual or paired working, whole-class discussions, collaborative group work, pair-work and peer evaluation. Computing is taught in a gradual, balanced and stimulating way across Pre-prep and Prep.
Physical Education
Physical Education
At Parsons Green Prep we understand that physical education is an important part of a child’s all-round development. PE lessons not only make for happy, healthy children; they also provide an opportunity to learn key life skills. They are designed to both stimulate and challenge our children. They are supported in the development of new skills and techniques and given the tools they need to succeed with competition. PE provides children with an opportunity to become independent learners and valuable team members. They learn to work together and develop an understanding of teamwork. We are inclusive and girls and boys may experience playing all the sports on the programme.

Indoor PE includes gymnastics. In addition to curriculum sport, we have an extensive list of sports clubs, which are run in the mornings and after school. Through these clubs, children can further develop their skills or try out entirely new sports, like table-tennis.
During the Pre-prep years, children learn basic core hand-eye skills to develop their coordination and spatial awareness. Core skills include throwing, catching and gymnastics. PE equipment is modified to complement ability and age levels. As the children move through the school, they are encouraged to participate in a team sport.
We believe it is important that every child has the opportunity to play sport competitively. Our school sports teams play against other local schools in tournaments and matches throughout the year. As members of the Independent Association of Prep Schools (IAPS) and Independent Schools Association (ISA), there are a number of tournaments and festivals of sport that we attend in West London. Over the past few years our teams have achieved impressive results in netball, football, skiing and tag rugby. We have also had success in athletics, where a number of children achieved medals in the sprints and long jump at the ISA West London athletics meet.
Every summer we hold a house swimming gala for Pre-prep and Prep and a sports day for the whole school, where all children are encouraged to take part and have fun. Sports day is a fantastic opportunity for parents to come along and see their children in action.

Open Day speech – Emily – Head of School
Hello and good morning. My name is Emily and I am honored to be Head Girl at Parsons Green Prep School. Today, I will share my favourite things about this amazing school!
I have been at Parsons Green Prep for over six years now and have not been disappointed. It is a school that I am so proud to be part of and I will be sad to leave next summer. If you choose to send your child here, then you will have all sorts of clubs to choose from, including debate club, which is my personal favourite, Irish Dancing, quiz club, coding, football and many more.
As well as the many clubs, there are a number of sports that every pupil takes part in. This term we have football or netball and can choose between the two. Next term we all take part in tag rugby and hockey, which is great fun! In the Summer term we play cricket and sometimes tennis, which we all love on a hot summer’s day. We particularly enjoy playing sports matches against other schools; sometimes we win and sometimes we lose, but of course it’s the taking part that counts. At the end of the year we have a spectacular sports day, where we dress up in our house colours and come out dripping in medals.
To give us energy for the various sports that we do, the school provides delicious lunches. We have excellent chefs who put in hard work every day to make sure we have an amazing lunch. On Fridays, we have an extra special treat lunch, with pizza, fries and my favourite – fish fingers! Throughout the week we are encouraged to eat a colourful rainbow plate of food which includes carbohydrates, protein, vegetables and dairy. After lunch, we all get a chance to play in our wonderful new playground. You will get a chance to see it when you wander around. Feel free to do a spot of climbing yourself!
Aside from the sports and clubs we enjoy, we have music and choir lessons every week. At the end of the school year, all years put on a fabulous school production. Last year our production was Robin Hood, but we have also performed Cinderella and Alice in Wonderland. I was a playing card! Every Christmas there is a wonderful Carol Concert in a local church, which we love taking part in.
One of the highlights of the school year is the residential trips, which pupils from Year 3 upwards take part in. My personal favourite trip was the trip to Mill on the Brue in Somerset. I got to jump off a two-story building – luckily I was attached to a harness! All pupils also enjoy various day trips throughout the year.
Our school is brilliant both academically and in many other ways. We are challenged but are always supported and are encouraged to do our very best. The teachers are preparing my class brilliantly for the 11+ process and making sure that we do not find anything too daunting. Everyone at our school is kind and welcoming and the teachers are always approachable. In such a small school, all the pupils get to know each other, which is really special. All Year 6 pupils have a ‘Reception buddy’, where we support their reading every Friday.
Speaking of reception, twice a year the older year groups team up with the Reception pupils and do a STEAM project. What is STEAM, I hear you ask. It stands for Science, Technology, Engineering, Art and Mathematics and is a very important part of the curriculum at PGP. One of our recent topics was DNA. We learnt about how DNA was discovered and how every person is unique.
I really hope you enjoy looking around our school this morning. I am so proud to be a pupil here. Thank you very much and have a lovely day!

Open Day speech – Axel – Head of School
Good morning to everyone. My name is Axel and I have the privilege to be one of the two Heads of School for Parsons Green Prep. I joined PGP in Reception six years ago and I have made wonderful memories and friends since then.
When I look back at my years at PGP I remember in particular the welcoming gates and the friendly atmosphere. I love this school because it feels like a village school but with a high focus on academic excellence with a London approach. The teachers here motivate and encourage one to stretch your academic and physical skills beyond your comfort zone. We have a ‘Marvellous Mistakes’ approach to learning, which means we acknowledge, value and sometimes even appreciate our mistakes as we learn from them and they can make us stronger.
At PGP we have a variety of different sports embedded into our curriculum and we also have many clubs to support our developing skills. Personally, my favourite clubs have been coding, debating and chess. A few years ago I won the whole school chess competition and was awarded a cup – I was thrilled. In sports we have lots of fixtures against other local schools, for instance in football, cricket, tag rugby and hockey. Did you know we also have a ski team who will be competing is the ISA competition next Monday?
I would also like to talk to you about our pastoral care here at PGP. We have an excellent kitchen chef and catering team. In my opinion the food is really delicious and the kitchen offers a multicultural menu made from scratch every day – even the bread.
We have also had residential trips every year starting from Year 3 and shorter days trips since Reception. To give you an example, my personal favourite so far has been our Year 4 trip to Mill on the Brue in Somerset. On this trip I loved tunnelling (that is going through dark tunnels with a headlamp) and our ‘leap of faith’ exercise. This experience helped build my resilience and determination to succeed.
Currently, my class is concentrating hard on upcoming 11+ exams. It is a bit nerve-racking because it is quite important for our senior school progression. But it has been very helpful that we have the same teacher for both Year 5 and Year 6. We also have extra booster sessions in the mornings. Like you, I am currently doing many of these Open Days at Senior Schools and hoping to find the right match for myself, so wish me luck!
I hope you will enjoy our Open Day tour today and I hope I can talk to many of you later today.
Thank you for listening to my speech.

Pastoral Care
Pastoral care is a co-pillar with academic achievement at PGP. Every child’s welfare is important to us and we aim to provide everyone with a happy and secure environment in which to learn and develop. Children are taught the value of good manners and mutual respect from the moment they arrive; they are kind and supportive to each other.
Teachers have primary responsibility for the wellbeing of the children in their class, both as individuals and as a group. Children are also aware of the many other adults they can go to if they need to, from the heads of pastoral care, pre-prep, teachers, assistants and the Head. The structure of our school allows children to make good friends across the classes and be known to all full-time teachers and assistants.
We take bullying very seriously and in the unlikely event that it does happen we always deal with it promptly and sensitively, in line with our Anti-Bullying Policy (click here to read it). We work closely with children, for example, through the Personal, Social, Health, Citizenship and Economic (PSHCE) education curriculum, allowing them to explore their feelings and to know that they have a voice. Our small classes, close relationships and open ethos allow children to share any concerns they may have.
